$comment: Machine-readable parameter contract for the projections named in api.md. The prose there stays the narrative; this file is what the implementations check against. Both languages carry the same table as a constant in their core (the core reads no files by design) and a test in each language asserts the constant equals this file — so the two cannot drift apart.

types.integer: a whole number. JSON knows no int/float split, so 2026 and 2026.0 are the same value and both are accepted; 2026.4 is a caller mistake, not a value to round into shape. Bounded to 2^53-1 so that both language runtimes represent it exactly.

rules.unknownParameter: A parameter that is not declared here is rejected with E_INPUT_INVALID. Silently ignoring it turns a misspelled `fiscalYear` on vatReturn into a plausible annual figure where a quarter was asked for.
rules.absentOptional: An undeclared-as-required parameter that is absent keeps its documented default. Absent is not the same as wrong.
rules.presentButInvalid: A declared parameter present with a value of the wrong type is rejected with E_INPUT_INVALID — never coerced, never defaulted.
rules.acceptedWithoutEffect: A parameter marked acceptedWithoutEffect is declared but read by no implementation. It is declared so the gap is visible instead of hiding behind a tolerant reader — NOT because it works, and each one is recorded as a finding. Resolve it by giving the parameter an effect or by retiring it in a new fixture; do not quietly bend an existing one. As of 2026-08-16 exactly one remains: balanceSheet.incomeMapping, and there by decision — see the comment on it.

incomeMapping.$comment: Stays without effect by decision, not by omission (IMPL-014, 2026-08-15). The result position sums income accounts by TYPE, and that is what makes the balance-sheet identity hold by construction (api.md); feeding it from a mapping would make the identity depend on that mapping being complete. The income statement carries the mapping's view, including the `_unassigned` catch-all, so both reports agree without this parameter doing anything.

format.$comment: Exactly one value is valid: "gobd-z3". It selects nothing (there is no second journal format) but it guards the caller: an unknown value used to be ignored, so you received the Z3 stream under whatever label you had typed and could ship it to an auditor as something else. Absent means gobd-z3.

fiscalYear.$comment: Must agree with the run named by runId, which already fixes it. Accepted and ignored before, so asking for one period and receiving another's numbers left no trace in the answer.

period.$comment: Must agree with the run named by runId — see fiscalYear.
